assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, turned atomic timekeeping into a regime of roughly 1e-18 fractional uncertainty. The idea is simple and original, and it is a precision instrument in the full sense. It underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and prospective redefinition of the second, and it extends the frequency-metrology line recognized in earlier prizes.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early Sr clocks. Ye's JILA group drove the systematic performance records and the many-body Sr lattice clock. The two-name configuration is clean and matches the supplied credit. I recall that other groups (for example PTB, NIST, SYRTE) also made important contributions, but they are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: clocks have been compared and reproduced across many laboratories over roughly two decades, with international roadmap activity toward a redefinition of the second. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Share of credit for the lattice-clock concept relative to ion-clock and optical-comb precedents is something I cannot verify independently.
Contributions by other lattice-clock groups are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos and then associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056, the active galaxy NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane. It required a kilometre-scale detector in Antarctic ice and is a strong experimental achievement in astroparticle physics. The result bears directly on cosmic-ray origins.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the principal driver of the concept and the collaboration. Karle contributed to detector construction, ice calibration and analysis. Yoshida is credited for the early AMANDA/IceCube efforts and high-energy analyses. The decisive work is a large-collaboration effort, so a three-person prize is a hard compromise and I cannot independently establish who should be included. The prize is for a discovery by a large instrument team.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the diffuse flux has been confirmed in several channels, and the point-source evidence has grown over time, although the individual source associations are at modest significance and the source population is still unresolved. KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD offer partial independent confirmation. I note that my own field is close to this one and I would weigh it with care.
uncertainties: Source identification is incomplete and several associations are at the 3-5 sigma level.
Attribution within a collaboration of hundreds is hard to settle.
Possible perception of proximity to my own research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates, and their later proposals for quantum simulation with cold atoms, created a concrete architecture for quantum information processing. It is a theory that was realized in experiments and now guides quantum technologies.
assessment.attribution: The two-person credit is natural for the joint proposal. The experimental realizations were by Wineland, Blatt and others; Wineland was already recognized in 2012, which weakens the case for double recognition. The B004 entry is theory-led, so the committee would have to be comfortable honouring theory enabling an already prized experimental field.
assessment.maturity: Mature: ion-trap gates and analog simulation have been realized in many laboratories for three decades, and the framework is a standard in the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion manipulation.
Boundary between this candidate and the optical-lattice simulation candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics gave a way of coupling superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, enabling readout and gates. It is the architecture behind much of today's superconducting quantum processors and is a pillar of quantum technologies. The idea is clear and the lasting impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf produced the 2004 theory and the first experiments. The supplied credit names four people, so any three-person limit leaves one significant contributor out. My choice of Wallraff, Schoelkopf and Girvin is a judgment call and Blais has a strong claim as the lead theorist.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the technical sense, with wide independent reproduction. Timing is complicated because the 2025 prize recognized superconducting circuit macroscopic quantum effects, which may reduce the appetite for another circuit prize so soon.
uncertainties: Who among four or more contributors is decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene combined a theoretical prediction of flat bands with experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it created the field of twistronics. The impact is large and the physics is novel.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald's 2011 theory predicted the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the 2018 experiments. The theory-plus-experiment trio is a natural configuration. Cao et al. had other co-authors and the contributions of other groups (for example the Dean and Young groups) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with replication by many groups, but the underlying mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so the interpretation is not stable.
uncertainties: Other candidate contributors fall outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts and the establishment of their cosmological distance settled a decades-old puzzle and made GRBs probes of the distant universe. The BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray instruments are an instrument-led breakthrough of the kind I know well from hard-X-ray and gamma-ray work.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB localizations and the first X-ray afterglow. The optical identification and redshift involved the van Paradijs team (van Paradijs is deceased) and Kulkarni's group in the radio and optical follow-up, with other groups also essential. A three-person prize is a hard fit to the real distribution of credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: the cosmological origin is firmly established and the field has progressed through Swift and Fermi to gravitational-wave counterparts. Timeliness is late rather than early.
uncertainties: Posthumous contributors and a distributed set of discoverers.
Which BeppoSAX and follow-up individuals are decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later giant effect in MgO barriers, enabled modern hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The discovery is a pillar of spintronics and builds on the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin's group advanced the MgO-based devices. Julliere's earlier low-temperature observation and the MgO theory and experiments from other groups mean credit is distributed, and the supplied three names may not cover everyone decisive.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent reproduction and large technological impact.
uncertainties: Partly engineering and materials progress, and the split among MgO contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire gain media and passive mode-locking made compact femtosecond lasers routine, enabling ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and attosecond science. The tool is of very high impact and complements the 1999, 2005 and 2023 prizes.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed the Ti:sapphire laser, Sibbett's group discovered Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller invented semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors. These are separate but complementary contributions, so the best three-person configuration is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely adopted, but the prize arguably comes late and has overlap with earlier prizes on ultrafast techniques.
uncertainties: Whether the originality is judged to be sufficiently separate from earlier ultrafast prizes.
Distinct contributions that may need different recognition.
